questions.q: When is Copy Journal the better choice over a recurring journal or allocation?
options: When an entry is only loosely similar to a past one, in a way a formula couldn't cleanly capture
When the entry repeats exactly the same way every period
When one pool needs to be split proportionally across many targets
When the journal needs to skip approval
questions.explain: Copy Journal suits irregular, one-off entries that resemble a past journal without fitting a standing automated definition.

questions.q: What status does a copied journal start in?
options: Posted, matching the original
Incomplete, regardless of the original journal's status
Approved automatically
Permanently Closed
questions.explain: A copy is a fresh draft that starts as Incomplete no matter what status the original journal had.

questions.q: Why might the accounting date need to be changed after copying a journal?
options: Dates can never be changed on a copy
Copied journals never need an accounting date
The original's period may now be closed, so a new date in a currently open period must be chosen
The date is automatically set to today regardless of input
questions.explain: Since the original's period may since have closed, the copy needs a valid date in a currently Open or Future Enterable period.

questions.q: Does copying a journal skip validation or approval?
options: Yes, copied journals bypass both validation and approval
It skips validation but still requires approval
It skips approval but still requires validation
No, a copied journal must balance, pass validation, and route through approval exactly like any other journal
questions.explain: Copying only saves retyping lines — it does not exempt the resulting journal from any of the usual controls.

questions.q: Which tool fits an exact same amount and accounts repeating every single period with no variation?
options: Copy Journal
Standard recurring journal
Skeleton recurring journal
Allocation
questions.explain: A Standard recurring journal is designed for entries where both the accounts and the amount never change.
